Anthropic shares close below IPO price as AI jitters return

Category: AI

Anthropic shares closed Tuesday at $81.91, down 6.5% and below the $83 IPO price for the first time, just four trading days after the Claude developer’s record-setting Nasdaq debut [31][11]. The stock opened at $111.50 on Nov. 19 and fell as low as $76.60 during Tuesday’s session; Reuters said the decline put nearly $200 billion in market value at risk [31]. Investors are reassessing AI companies’ valuations and computing infrastructure costs, with higher interest rates adding to financing concerns [31][82]. Anthropic also missed Monday’s rally in AI shares after Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive. On Tuesday, the Nasdaq fell 1.5% and the S&P 500 lost 0.5%, while the Dow rose 0.9% [31][82]. Separately, Business Insider and MarketWatch reported that employees at Anthropic and rival OpenAI have questioned internally whether the companies can safely release their most powerful unreleased models [4][7]. Anthropic said it recently delayed pretraining a new frontier model for more than a month to strengthen security [7].

Primary Source: View original article

If we do see a slowdown in the data-center buildout, then that obviously can impact the speed at which Anthropic can develop and therefore future revenue and therefore its valuation

— Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX (News18 (Reuters))

Did you know: About 5,100 of Anthropic’s roughly 5,300 employees held equity stakes valued above $1 million after the first day of trading, according to Meduza [67].

Key Points

  • Index inclusion: MSCI is scheduled to add Anthropic to its global standard indexes after the Nov. 30 close; one analysis estimated passive-fund demand could equal 30% of the IPO shares by year-end [74].
  • Chip tracking: A bill promoted by Senate Intelligence Committee Chairman Tom Cotton would require chipmakers to track advanced AI processors and notify the government if they suspect chips have reached prohibited users [216].
  • Executive sale: A filing showed CEO Dario Amodei sold more than 3.37 million shares worth about $280 million to IPO underwriters as part of the offering, rather than on the open market [16].
  • AI model debate: The White House supports open-weight AI models, whose components can be downloaded and adapted. These models can broaden demand for Nvidia computing beyond a few leading model developers; Anthropic and OpenAI have questioned their implications [165].
  • Institutional allocation: About half of the institutional investors who placed orders for the IPO received no shares; those firms did not appear to be rushing to buy on the pullback [24].
  • Options activity: Nearly 500,000 options contracts traded by noon Tuesday, carrying about $250 million in premiums; puts outnumbered calls roughly 300,000 to 200,000, while large trades suggested divided views [1].
  • IPO supply: The Financial Times reported that underwriters exercised the full greenshoe option after one trading day, raising another $12.2 billion, while 315 million non-founder insider shares were eligible for sale from day one [72].

Perspectives

Wedbush Securities: Analyst Ygal Arounian rated the stock Outperform with a $120 target, arguing that frontier AI could serve the much larger knowledge-work market rather than just traditional software budgets. He estimated Anthropic’s market penetration at less than 1%.

Sources: CNBC

CFRA Research: Equity analyst Janice Quek maintained a Buy rating, saying customers continued to use Anthropic’s services despite cheaper AI products, while warning that growing competition from open-weight models remained a risk.

Sources: Cnyes

Arisa Liu, a research fellow at Taiwan Industry Economics Services, said Huang’s personal ties to Taiwan remove a perceived risk that a successor might weaken Nvidia’s relationship with the island’s chip supply chain [147].

Sources: South China Morning Post

Timeline

  • 19 November 2026: Anthropic began Nasdaq trading after pricing shares at $83 [31].
  • 23 November 2026: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, lifting AI shares [63][82].
  • 24 November 2026: Anthropic closed below its IPO price for the first time [31][11].
  • 30 November 2026: MSCI inclusion in global standard indexes is scheduled after the close [74].
  • 12 November 2026: Huang resigned after Nvidia’s board accepted his departure [242]
  • 23 November 2026: Nvidia’s board reinstated Huang as CEO and president [120]
  • 24 November 2026: Huang addressed employees at his first all-hands meeting since his return [14]
  • 1 December 2026: Huang is scheduled for closed-door interviews with three House committees [188]
  • 3 December 2026: Huang is scheduled to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee [227]

Industry Impact

  • Taiwan chip supply chain: Huang’s reinstatement helped lift Taiwan’s benchmark Taiex nearly 9%, while analysts said the island’s manufacturers could attract additional orders if US scrutiny redirects Nvidia business from mainland China [147].
  • AI infrastructure finance: Nvidia’s loans to and investments in major customers helped support the AI buildout, so leadership uncertainty raised concerns beyond its role as a chip supplier [149].

Historical Background

Reuters cited two prominent comparisons with Anthropic’s early drop below its offer price: SpaceX took about a month to fall below its IPO price [31]. Facebook, now Meta Platforms, fell below its offer price on its second trading day in 2012 [31].

Business Angle

  • Monitor whether Anthropic sustains its progress on free cash flow: Man Group said the company was already bringing in cash and was close to breaking even on free cash flow [86].
  • Track whether management can explain the slowdown in sequential revenue growth: Seaport Research’s Jay Goldberg cited a decline from 144% in the second quarter to 44% in the third [9].

Q&A

Q: What investigations involving Nvidia remain open?

A: Nvidia’s independent-director inquiry is continuing, the Justice Department is investigating alleged chip diversion through Megaspeed, and the SEC has reportedly examined the company’s accounting practices and shareholder communications [188].

Analysts urge independent code safeguards for Anthropic's Claude Ship

Category: AI

Software analysts and engineers are urging caution over Anthropic’s Claude Ship, a beta service that reviews GitHub code changes, fixes problems and can approve routine pull requests under team-written policies. The service combines Code Review with two beta agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, to assess whether code is ready to merge [6][14]. Analysts warn that AI systems that generate and review code may share blind spots, while automated approvals could leave teams unclear about who is accountable for a faulty change. Deepika Giri, IDC vice president for Asia/Pacific artificial-intelligence platforms and advisory, said teams should keep security scans and continuous-integration checks independent of the AI reviewer and assign a human owner to every merge [6]. Nitish Tyagi, a senior principal analyst at Gartner, said models’ non-determinism makes them unsuitable as the sole quality gate [6]. Anthropic recommends running approvals first in observe-only mode, where the agent reports decisions without blocking or approving merges. The company cited results from its Claude Code team but said Claude review was one layer in a broader process. Analysts say teams should assess deployments by tracking defects and rework as well as delivery speed [17][15][6].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

AI models are inherently non-deterministic, which makes them unsuitable as the sole quality gate

— Nitish Tyagi, senior principal analyst at Gartner (InfoWorld)

Key Points

  • Usage costs: Claude Ship charges by token use. Costs depend on pull-request size and volume, review depth and PR Steward’s repair work; administrators can cap Code Review and PR Steward spending [17][6].
  • Access limits: The beta supports GitHub repositories for Claude Team and Enterprise customers but excludes organizations using Zero Data Retention, HIPAA configurations or customer-managed encryption keys [3][17].
  • Platform competition: Omdia analyst Lian Jye Su said Claude Ship may appeal to existing Claude Code customers, while IDC’s Deepika Giri noted that GitHub and GitLab benefit from tighter integration with their own development platforms [6].
  • Pilot feedback: Carvana engineering executive Alex Devkar said the PR Steward pilot reduced time spent processing review feedback and allowed teams to tailor how it suggests and organizes changes [17].
  • Benchmarking: IDC’s Deepika Giri recommended tracking spending per merged pull request, cycle time, change-failure rates, reversions and developer satisfaction before expanding beyond an initial repository [6].

Perspectives

Deepika Giri, IDC vice president for Asia/Pacific artificial-intelligence platforms and advisory: Giri warned that code-generating and code-reviewing models may share blind spots; she recommended limiting automated approvals to low-risk changes, retaining independent security checks and assigning a human owner to every merge [6].

Sources: InfoWorld

Nitish Tyagi, Gartner senior principal analyst: Tyagi said AI’s non-deterministic behavior means it should not serve as the only quality gate, and recommended distinct agent identities linked to the developer or team accountable for a pull request [6].

Sources: InfoWorld

Lian Jye Su, Omdia chief analyst: Su said Anthropic’s integration with Claude Code could attract enterprises already using its coding tools, but warned agents may not fully account for changing security and compliance requirements in some industries [6].

Sources: InfoWorld

Carvana engineering team: Senior Vice President of Engineering and Analytics Alex Devkar said its pilot helped teams spend less time addressing review feedback and allowed the tool to be adapted to their existing process [17].

Sources: Help Net Security

Timeline

  • 9 March 2026: Anthropic introduced Code Review as a research preview [33]
  • 15 October 2026: Code Review became generally available [33]
  • 23 November 2026: Anthropic announced Claude Ship and began its beta rollout [33]
  • 15 January 2027: Eligible Enterprise customers can claim credits through this deadline [17]

Technical Details

  • Approval versus merge: Claude Approvals can issue an approval decision, but a merge still depends on GitHub branch-protection rules, required checks and the developer’s permissions [3][14].
  • Repository policy file: Approval policy is stored in the repository and activates when the file reaches the default branch; teams can combine Code Review findings with custom natural-language classifiers [17][3].

Historical Background

A peer-reviewed study cited by Decrypt found OpenAI and Anthropic models performed slightly better at identifying and repairing vulnerabilities in human-written code than in AI-generated code [15]. In April, a startup founder reported that a Claude coding agent deleted a production database and its volume-level backups through one API call [15]. An October engineering report described a proposed change that went through more than 50 automated review-and-correction rounds overnight before its author intervened [15].

Business Angle

  • A higher merge count is not enough to prove savings if defects and rework rise alongside delivery speed [6].
  • Token consumption varies with pull-request volume, size, review depth and the repairs performed, so buyers need repository-level cost controls [6][17].

Q&A

Q: What credit offer is available to some enterprise customers?

A: Eligible Claude Enterprise organizations can claim at least $10,000 in usage credits by January 15, 2027, and must use them within 30 days of claiming [17][3].

item.content:encoded:
Anthropic lets Claude users install AI-built tools as Mac and Windows apps

Category: AI

Anthropic has begun rolling out “Install as app,” a beta feature that turns eligible tools created with its Claude chatbot into desktop apps for macOS and Windows. The apps have their own icons and windows, can be shared, and can use Claude connectors. Users can build them by describing a tool in a chat, without packaging code or setting up an API key [1][3][14][17]. The apps require an internet connection and an active Claude sign-in to open, and Claude requests count against the user’s plan limits [9][5][17]. Anthropic does not review apps before installation, and users decide whether to grant access to desktop features or local files [3][14]. The beta is rolling out across Claude plans, but it is limited to the Mac and Windows desktop clients; template-based Docs, Slides and Sheets artifacts cannot be installed [3][5]. Team administrators can control full computer access, while Enterprise owners must enable the feature. Anthropic has also cautioned that users should grant broad access only to apps from authors they trust [3][17].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Key Points

  • Permission tiers: Apps start with browser-level capabilities. Separate permissions can enable notifications, global shortcuts or floating windows, while full access lets apps run programs and read, change or delete files [14][3].
  • Update exposure: Claude requests permission again after an artifact update, but code loaded from an external website can change without prompting for renewed approval [5][15].
  • Shared app use: People using a shared app that calls Claude sign in with their own accounts, and usage counts against their plans, not the creator’s [3].
  • Admin controls: Team plans allow installation by default but keep full computer access off until an administrator enables it; Enterprise plans have the feature disabled by default [3][2].
  • Organizational exclusions: HIPAA-ready and hybrid deployments cannot use the apps; full computer access is also unavailable to Claude for Teachers and K–12 organizations [3][5].

Perspectives

Anthropic: The company says tools people rely on for work should open like other apps and notify users when something needs attention [12].

Sources: SiliconANGLE

AppleInsider: The Apple-focused technology publication argues that mandatory internet access and Claude sign-in make the apps less useful than conventional desktop software, which can work offline [9].

Sources: AppleInsider

Technical Details

  • Client requirement: Installing an artifact as an app requires Claude Desktop for Mac or Windows version 6.28899.0 or later [3][5].
  • Authorship limits: Full computer access is generally limited to apps the user created or, for Team and Enterprise customers, apps made within their organization [14][3].

item.content:encoded:
Tidal to begin removing fully AI-generated music Dec. 9

Category: AI

Tidal says its systems flagged 43% of tracks delivered in the past 90 days as wholly AI-generated, with 94% of its AI-tagged catalog attributed to Suno, a music-generation platform [5][17]. The streaming service will begin removing fully AI-generated tracks on Dec. 9 and block new deliveries, while continuing to accept music made with AI assistance [6][7]. Tidal will use detection technology from Ircam Amplify, a French music-technology company, and screen submission metadata to distinguish fully generated recordings from work involving human creative input [12][4]. A Tidal spokesperson told Rolling Stone that most appeals it reviewed upheld the AI classification, while acknowledging that some false positives are inevitable [7]. Pitchfork reported that Ircam Amplify advertises 99% accuracy and a 1% false-positive rate, and estimated that applying that rate to the takedown could mistakenly flag about 290,000 songs [15]. The policy is stricter than the labeling systems used by Spotify and Apple Music. Bandcamp also bars AI music under a broader rule covering work made substantially with AI [26][22]. Tidal expects to finish removing the tracks by early 2027 [5].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

We are the first DSP to do so, and we encourage our peers to follow suit.

— Robert Anderson, Tidal lead at Block (Gizmodo)

Did you know: Apple Music vice president Oliver Schusser said fully AI-generated tracks made up more than a third of monthly uploads to the service but accounted for less than 0.5% of listening [28].

Key Points

  • Low listening: Tidal said 96% of its AI-generated songs received zero plays in the previous 90 days [5][6].
  • Demand mismatch: Apple Music executive Oliver Schusser said more than a third of monthly uploads were fully AI-generated, while such music accounted for less than 0.5% of listening [28][32].
  • Daily rejections: Tidal expects to reject 80,000 to 85,000 songs a day once the ban takes effect [5][6].
  • Listener survey: An Ipsos survey across nine countries found 57% of respondents had fully AI-generated music in their playlists, while 74% thought they did not [16].
  • Rival policies: Spotify says it removed more than 75 million spam tracks from its catalog and 50 million from recommendations, while continuing to allow labeled AI music [5][42].
  • Impersonation removals: Tidal says it has already removed more than 65,000 tracks flagged for suspected artist-name impersonation [13][1].
  • Rival responses: Spotify said it removed 50 million spam tracks from recommendations and deleted 75 million spam tracks from its catalog, while retaining labels and other measures rather than a blanket ban [13][26].
  • Suno concentration: Tidal data cited by Digital Trends attributes 94% of its AI-badged tracks to Suno, a generative AI music platform [17].

Perspectives

Tidal: The company argues that the volume of unplayed AI uploads buries human artists and creates risks of impersonation and diverted royalties [13].

Music-industry organizations: Eight groups say distinguishing AI-generated recordings from AI-assisted work protects listeners’ ability to know how music was made [30].

Sources: iThome

Spotify: The company says its effort to limit AI spam is ongoing and that bad actors adapt quickly. It also expects listeners to value human artistry as AI makes music more abundant [5].

Sources: Variety

Universal Music Group CEO Lucian Grainge: Grainge has argued that streaming services should pay less for AI-generated tracks than for human-made music, saying synthetic uploads can degrade the listening experience and shift value away from artists [46].

Sources: The Hollywood Reporter

Tidal: A company spokesperson said Tidal expects some false positives from its detection partner, Ircam Amplify, but described its review and appeal process as safeguards. The spokesperson said most appeals so far had upheld the original detection [7].

Sources: Rolling Stone

Timeline

  • 29 June 2026: Tidal introduced labeling and royalty restrictions for wholly AI-made tracks [18]
  • 10 July 2026: Eight music groups announced a voluntary AI-music labeling standard [30]
  • 6 November 2026: Tidal said AI-made music exceeded 60% of that day’s deliveries [4]
  • 9 December 2026: Tidal is scheduled to begin removing fully AI-generated tracks [6]
  • January 2026: Bandcamp announced a ban on wholly or substantially AI-generated music [22]
  • July 2026: Tidal began labeling wholly AI-generated tracks and making them ineligible for royalties [6]
  • 6 November 2026: More than 60% of Tidal submissions that day were AI-generated [46]
  • 24 November 2026: Tidal announced removals and a ban on future wholly AI-generated uploads [5]
  • 9 December 2026: Tidal is scheduled to start removing existing wholly AI-generated music [5]
  • 2027: Tidal expects to finish removing existing wholly AI-generated tracks by the start of the year [5]

Technical Details

  • Detection and metadata checks: Tidal plans to combine detection technology from Ircam Amplify with checks of distributor metadata. Metadata identifying a track as generated solely with AI can trigger rejection [4][46].
  • Detection accuracy claims: Ircam Amplify advertises 99% accuracy and a 1% false-positive rate [15].

Industry Impact

  • Record-label revenue: Labels are pursuing deals with platforms and AI developers to license catalogs for training or remixing; Goldman Sachs estimated related licensing and monetization opportunities could lift label revenue by 10% by 2035 [6].
  • Streaming platforms: Deezer uses detection to label fully AI-generated tracks and keep them out of recommendations and editorial playlists, while planning a listener control to hide them [26].
  • Music distribution: Tidal expects to reject 80,000 to 85,000 tracks a day once the new rules take effect [5].

Historical Background

Tidal’s June policy covered music described as “wholly or substantially” generated by AI, while the current removal rule covers tracks generated entirely by AI [15].

Business Angle

  • Tidal says a small number of false positives are inevitable and says it has an appeals process. Pitchfork reported that it asked Tidal what recourse artists would have [7][15].

item.content:encoded:
UK watchdog warns AI agents handling finances may need regulatory approval

Category: AI

Britain’s Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) warned technology and social media companies on Nov. 24 that AI agents may need regulatory authorization for activities involving payments, financial promotions or advice. The warning coincided with Meta’s UK launch of its Muse assistant. Meta says Muse can renew car insurance, pursue refunds and make online purchases, but the UK version cannot access bank balances or provide personalized financial guidance. Muse has surpassed 10 million downloads since its September US launch [9][5]. The FCA said regulatory obligations depend on what an agent does, not whether its operator calls itself a technology company, and urged developers to engage with regulators early [9][4]. Firms using AI remain responsible for compliance even when they rely on outside providers. Consumers should check what protections apply and what personal information they share [6][5]. A separate UK regulatory consultation on controls for AI systems remains open until Feb. 26, 2027 [10].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

We’ve engaged constructively with the appropriate regulatory authorities and will continue to do so.

— Meta spokesperson (WTVB (Reuters))

Key Points

  • Operational controls: The FCA expects regulated firms to understand agents’ autonomy and risks and maintain controls that work in real time and under stress [8][7].
  • AI governance: Firms should track approved AI use cases in formal inventories and prevent or detect unapproved tools and software built with AI assistance [10].
  • Bank concerns: Banks have already urged the FCA to scrutinize AI chatbots giving financial advice to consumers [9].

Perspectives

Meta: The company says it wants to connect Muse to UK banking services only after consulting regulators and obtaining any required licences [9].

Sources: Reuters

Timeline

  • September 2026: Meta launched Muse in the United States [9].
  • 24 November 2026: The FCA published its warning and Meta launched Muse in the UK [9].
  • 26 February 2027: The consultation on proposed AI controls is scheduled to close [10].

Business Angle

  • Operational readiness: Firms may need to maintain inventories of autonomous agents, document decision thresholds and action limits, and maintain real-time safeguards [1].
  • Informational assistants and agents that execute transactions or make financial decisions face different regulatory exposure [9][1].

Q&A

Q: What can the FCA do if a company offers regulated services without authorization?

A: The regulator says it can intervene against firms conducting regulated financial activities without the required authorization [6][4].

Q: Will the FCA provide a route for testing agentic products?

A: The FCA says its AI Lab supports development and testing, and it plans an Agentic Policy Sprint for firms, policymakers and technology providers [6].

item.content:encoded:
Take-Two removes 3,007 repositories for GTA 6 PC port

Category: Technology

Take-Two Interactive, the parent company of Rockstar Games, used a Digital Millennium Copyright Act notice to take down Project Leonida, an unofficial effort to run Grand Theft Auto VI on PC, across 3,007 GitHub repositories containing its code [1][14]. The company said the project facilitated copyright infringement because it was built to run leaked Xbox game files. It rejected the developers’ instruction for users to “bring your own files” as “intentionally misleading” [1]. The project’s administrator, NotRexed, said its Discord server had also been taken down and ended development [15][5]. The takedown followed the circulation of an Xbox game build and a key executable, which accelerated attempts to recompile the game for Windows and other systems [8][20]. Leonida had reached the game’s setup screen, but footage showed a black screen afterward, not a playable port [25][16]. Other teams are still working on unofficial versions, using AI coding tools to help reverse-engineer the leaked files [2][24]. Rockstar has not announced a PC release date. A report cited by several publications points to the first quarter of 2027, but that timing is unconfirmed [13][24].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Rockstar taking my server down was only part of the reason. Like I've said before, I'm a 15 year-old kid. Managing school and sports is hard enough without having middle aged men yell and complain to you on Discord. Goodbye.

— NotRexed, Project Leonida administrator (Eurogamer)

Key Points

  • Leonida’s developers estimated it could take about a week to produce a playable build after the leaked executable appeared [16][25].
  • Community shutdowns: Tom’s Hardware reported that Leonida’s Discord server had nearly 180,000 members and that Discord had banned its project account for two years [5].
  • Progress elsewhere: PortWatch VI ranked a group called CGBJ first, drawing on progress from XCL and Victory [8].

Perspectives

Cyberleek, who leaked GTA 6 files, described their release as opposition to what they called anti-consumer practices in the games industry. GameSpot reported, however, that the executable’s release had previously been tied to a cryptocurrency token target [16].

Sources: GameSpot

Timeline

  • 19 November 2026: Grand Theft Auto VI launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series consoles [5][11]
  • 20 November 2026: Take-Two said leaked Xbox-build files were publicly distributed [1]
  • 21 November 2026: The Leonida repository opened to run the Xbox build on PC [3]
  • 23 November 2026: Cyberleek released the Xbox build executable, accelerating porting attempts [20][1]
  • 23 November 2026: GitHub processed Take-Two’s takedown across 3,007 repositories [1][14]

Technical Details

  • Static recompilation: This approach translates console code into a native PC version rather than emulating the full console system. Leonida pursued recompilation of the leaked Xbox build [12][2].
  • Emulation: Other groups are attempting to run the Xbox game through an emulation layer on PC rather than recompiling the code to run natively [12][2].
  • Some demonstrations progressed beyond booting: Modders showed a third-person view of Lucia in the prison prologue with shaders rendered, but the game ran at only a few frames per second and had persistent graphical faults [17].

Historical Background

Take-Two had been pursuing the source of the GTA VI leaks for months. In August 2026, it sought subpoenas for data from Discord and Microsoft, which owns GitHub, that could help identify Cyberleek [20].

Action Items

  • Avoid unofficial GTA VI PC installers: Do not download purported working PC builds from unfamiliar sites. Security warnings in the reporting say some fake installers contain malware [12][17].

item.author: Kite Feed Generator (Technology / Cloud Reliability)
item.description: Microsoft has launched an internal “Code Red” overhaul after a Nov. 12-13 failure disrupted Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services for about 24 hours. The company aims to resolve future global incidents within one hour [15][6]. Microsoft attributed the outage to a Windows scalability defect introduced in July and said neither cyber activity nor AI agents caused it. The disruption affected government agencies, trading firms and airline communications across several countries [15][23]. The company’s review found that diagnostic information scattered across internal systems hampered its response: engineers exchanged more than 11,000 messages in 11 Teams chats without maintaining a single shared view of the incident [15][4]. Microsoft plans to limit system load, separate traffic by region and speed recovery, with AI agents intended to help engineers interpret system-health data [15]. The company has not said when it expects to meet the one-hour target. Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core, will hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team and weekly reviews. In a separate recent incident, an urgent fix took five to six days to reach users worldwide [15][6].

Microsoft launches Code Red after outage, sets one-hour recovery goal

Category: Technology

Microsoft has launched an internal “Code Red” overhaul after a Nov. 12-13 failure disrupted Exchange Online, Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 services for about 24 hours. The company aims to resolve future global incidents within one hour [15][6]. Microsoft attributed the outage to a Windows scalability defect introduced in July and said neither cyber activity nor AI agents caused it. The disruption affected government agencies, trading firms and airline communications across several countries [15][23]. The company’s review found that diagnostic information scattered across internal systems hampered its response: engineers exchanged more than 11,000 messages in 11 Teams chats without maintaining a single shared view of the incident [15][4]. Microsoft plans to limit system load, separate traffic by region and speed recovery, with AI agents intended to help engineers interpret system-health data [15]. The company has not said when it expects to meet the one-hour target. Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core, will hold daily meetings with the Substrate leadership team and weekly reviews. In a separate recent incident, an urgent fix took five to six days to reach users worldwide [15][6].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team

— Jason Henderson, president of Microsoft 365 Core (Reuters)

Key Points

  • Failure history: Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna said the affected component had accumulated “roughly ten years’ worth of acceptable failures,” according to a memo by Amanda Silver [15].
  • Patch goal: Jason Henderson said Microsoft wants its most urgent security fixes safely deployed worldwide within an hour of detection [15][10].

Perspectives

Satya Nadella, Microsoft's chief executive, said better software testing and stronger system isolation could have prevented the disruption [23].

Sources: To Vima

Brad Smith, Microsoft president, warned that more technology outages could occur in the coming months, saying AI has accelerated the discovery of weaknesses in computer code and that the infrastructure update will take more than weeks to complete [11].

Sources: Free Press Journal

Timeline

  • July 2026: Windows scalability defect introduced, later blamed for the outage [15][23]
  • 31 August 2026: A separate outage knocked critical Microsoft services offline [23]
  • 12 November 2026: Microsoft 365 service disruption began, affecting users internationally [15][23]
  • 15 November 2026: Microsoft's preliminary report attributed the downtime to a Windows defect [14]
  • 18 November 2026: Satya Nadella apologized and discussed testing and isolation improvements [23]
  • 20 November 2026: Henderson's memo called the disruption Exchange Online's most impactful incident [15]
  • 23 November 2026: Amanda Silver described fragmented diagnostics and the response's “fog of war” [15]
  • 24 November 2026: Reuters reported Microsoft's Code Red overhaul and one-hour recovery target [15]

Technical Details

  • Gateway lock contention: Microsoft's post-incident account traced the outage to a scalability flaw that caused lock contention in gateway processes. About 15 hours before the outage, a Teams failover shifted traffic to a gateway shared with Exchange Online, while maintenance had taken nearly 14% of gateway capacity offline [6][23].
  • Regional failover limits: The primary gateway's failure left more than 80% of its servers unresponsive, and Exchange Online could not switch to another gateway as some other services did [23].
  • Recovery sequence: Teams, SharePoint and OneDrive partially recovered before Exchange Online, but features that depended on Exchange could still be affected [7].

Industry Impact

  • Public services: Immigration New Zealand halted processing of all visa applications during the outage; police, health services, courts, businesses and schools in the UK were also affected [23].

Q&A

Q: Will outside reviewers assess Microsoft's Code Red changes?

A: Microsoft has not said whether external reviews will be involved [26].

Action Items

  • Test essential workflows without Microsoft 365: Have your technology team rehearse a critical task—such as payroll approval—without Outlook or Teams, and confirm that staff can access contact lists, runbooks and status updates through separate channels [7].
  • Check eligibility for service credits: Review the Microsoft 365 service-level agreement for your subscription to see whether availability fell below its targets [8].

Nothing sets December 8 launch for AI recording earbuds

Category: Technology

Nothing will unveil its Ear (note) wireless earbuds on December 8, combining phone-call recording through the earbuds with in-person conversation recording through microphones in the charging case [2][3][11]. A companion app will manage recordings, transcripts and summaries. The earbuds are designed to work with multiple AI agents and Nothing’s own voice-control system [5][9]. Users can place the case on a meeting table to record conversations without a separate recorder or phone app, while the earbuds capture phone calls [3][8]. Nothing has not set a price or disclosed full specifications [5][6][2]. CEO Carl Pei said Nothing approached recording cautiously because of consent and privacy concerns. Reports on the preview also noted that the company had consulted law firms and created a London data-security team [6][11]. Nothing is due to provide more product details at the December 8 launch [2][10].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

AI is only as useful as what it knows about you. This is the first of many products building a hardware context layer for AI.

— Nothing CEO Carl Pei (Ubergizmo)

Key Points

  • Privacy questions: At the preview, Nothing had not clarified whether recordings would trigger a notice to the other person or whether transcription would run on-device or in the cloud [3][7].
  • Button controls: The case has dedicated Talk and recording controls, and Nothing is considering letting users reassign the Talk button to other functions [6][5].
  • Pei’s outlook: Pei said consumer AI devices are likely to remain niche in the near term and that he does not expect an iPhone-like breakthrough soon [11][14].

Perspectives

Nothing: The company says it obtained privacy certifications comparable to those of competing recording products [6].

Sources: Neowin

Workplace IT teams: TechRepublic advises organizations to test whether users can notify participants, control access and sharing, and delete audio, transcripts and summaries before allowing the device in workplace meetings [8].

Sources: TechRepublic

Timeline

  • 10 November 2026: Nothing teased its screenless AI device ahead of naming it [2].
  • 23 November 2026: Carl Pei described the product as part of an AI hardware context layer [2].
  • 24 November 2026: Nothing demonstrated Ear (note) and its recording functions to Bloomberg [11][5].
  • 8 December 2026: Nothing plans to announce product specifications and launch details [2].

Technical Details

  • Phone-independent recording: Nothing says the device can record audio without staying connected to a paired smartphone [2].
  • The charging case has two LED status lights [6].

Industry Impact

  • AI recording devices: The product enters a field that includes Plaud and Amazon Bee, while Nothing is combining call capture and in-person recording in one earbuds-and-case system [7][11].

Historical Background

Nothing had already experimented with AI access through earbuds: about two years before the Ear (note) preview, it added ChatGPT integration to its Ear and Ear A models [4]. The Ear (3) also included a physical button on the case for recording conversations. The new product expands that feature to case-based meeting recording [2][7].

Business Angle

  • Subscription terms: Nothing had not clarified whether access to the AI features would involve recurring costs [7].

Q&A

Q: What recording consent rules apply in Germany?

A: Heise reports that German law requires consent from everyone involved before a private conversation or phone call is recorded; violations can bring up to three years in prison or a fine [14].

Q: Where will Nothing sell the Ear (note)?

A: Nothing had not confirmed the product’s global availability or launch markets [10].

item.content:encoded:
Nvidia CEO Huang apologizes to staff as Trump floats pardon

Category: World

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang apologized to employees on Tuesday, acknowledged violating the company’s conduct rules and said he is in therapy. He returned as CEO a day earlier, 11 days after resigning over disclosures of affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence suspects of having ties to Chinese intelligence. That relationship became entangled with an investigation into whether Nvidia chips were diverted to China through Singapore-based customer Megaspeed [12][75]. At a company-wide meeting at Nvidia’s Santa Clara headquarters, Huang said it was “not acceptable” that he had broken rules he helped write. He denied that pressure from President Donald Trump had secured his reinstatement, saying the board had evaluated the facts. Trump has said he personally convinced directors to reinstate Huang. Attorney General Todd Blanche declined on Tuesday to confirm whether federal authorities had investigated Huang and described Nvidia as a “good corporate citizen” [12][54][75]. Trump told the New York Post a pardon was “always an option” but likely unnecessary, and urged Huang to tell the truth when he appears before lawmakers. Huang is scheduled for closed-door House interviews on Dec. 1 and a public Senate hearing on Dec. 3 [4][myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com#1]. Nvidia shares fell about 6% Tuesday after rising more than 31% Monday. The company’s internal inquiry and government inquiries remain active [12][2].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

I made some terrible mistakes

— Jensen Huang, Nvidia CEO (South China Morning Post)

Key Points

  • Board scrutiny: Governance experts said the board’s reversal after publicly rejecting Huang’s return raises questions about its independence and enforcement of Nvidia’s conduct rules [76][111].
  • Spending outlook: Brian Levitt, chief global market strategist at Invesco, said Nvidia’s substantial cash flow could allow many AI-industry investments to continue, though investment and earnings growth were unlikely to return to their first-half pace [12].
  • China shipments: Nvidia said it halted shipments to China of U.S.-licensed Hopper chips, including the H200; analysts said Huang’s return does not change export restrictions [2].
  • Other inquiries: California’s attorney general has opened an investigation into Nvidia’s chip exports and shareholder disclosures, while a reported SEC accounting inquiry adds another line of scrutiny [myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com#1][70].
  • Board oversight: Governance experts note that exchange rules require a majority-independent board, while one expert said long director tenures can undermine independence [1][7].
  • Export proposals: Lawmakers may seek to add export-control measures to the annual defense policy bill during the lame-duck session; proposals include restrictions on advanced chips and chipmaking tools, as well as location verification [118].
  • Supplier exposure: The earlier rebound lifted Taiwan’s TSMC and South Korea’s Samsung and SK Hynix, along with other chipmakers and equipment suppliers across Asia [92][124].
  • Market warning: Charles Schwab strategist Joe Mazzola said one strong session does not establish a market bottom, with investors also pricing in a possible Federal Reserve rate increase [84].

Perspectives

President Donald Trump: Trump said he had considered having the U.S. government take a stake in Nvidia, adding that it was “probably not too late” [4].

Sources: NDTV

Sen. Elizabeth Warren: The Massachusetts Democrat said she did not trust Nvidia’s internal investigation or Trump’s account of examining Huang, and called for congressional scrutiny [43].

Sources: 41NBC

Kathleen Day, Johns Hopkins Carey Business School lecturer: Day argued that Nvidia’s directors owe their duty to shareholders rather than the CEO and said shareholders should demand a new board [1].

Sources: Japan Today

Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Markets, said Huang’s return restores strategic continuity and reduces the immediate risk of supply-chain disruption. She said his relationships across the industry are difficult to replicate.

Sources: Euronews

Timeline

  • 12 November 2026: Huang resigned as CEO after conduct disclosures [32][65]
  • 17 November 2026: Nvidia’s chairman said the board would not reinstate Huang [65]
  • 23 November 2026: The board voted unanimously to restore Huang as CEO [2][1]
  • 24 November 2026: Huang apologized to staff and disclosed his therapy [12][27]
  • 1 December 2026: Huang is scheduled for closed-door interviews with three House committees [myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com#1]
  • 3 December 2026: Huang is due at a public Senate committee hearing [myrepublica.nagariknetwork.com#1]
  • 8 November 2026: Nvidia launched an independent investigation into the allegations [89]
  • 17 November 2026: Chair Harvey Jones said the board did not plan to reinstate Huang [89]
  • 24 November 2026: Nvidia fell nearly 6% as its post-reinstatement rally reversed [56]

Industry Impact

  • AI investment vehicles: SoftBank shares fell as much as 17% Wednesday to a 52-week low as investors questioned the costs and returns of its AI bets; the stock had lost nearly 70% from its June peak [84].

Historical Background

The U.S. Commerce and Justice departments said they began investigating Megaspeed in 2024 for potential export-control violations [75].

Business Angle

  • CoreWeave borrows to buy Nvidia chips and rents computing space; it lost hundreds of millions of dollars last quarter after interest payments [46].
  • The board voted unanimously to reinstate Huang, while Nvidia’s internal inquiry and government inquiries remain active [1][12].
  • Huang said Nvidia’s investments in AI startups that then bought its chips financed genuine demand, defending the practice against concerns about circular financing [39].

Q&A

Q: What new company-level safeguard has Nvidia announced?

A: Nvidia said a board committee will oversee national-security and export-control risks while its internal investigation continues [68].

Q: When will lawmakers question Huang, and what form will the hearings take?

A: Huang is scheduled for a closed-door interview with three House panels on Dec. 1 and public testimony before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3 [86][118].

US jury convicts Huawei on 10 counts; sentencing set for 2027

Category: World

A federal jury in Brooklyn found Chinese telecommunications company Huawei guilty on 10 of 12 criminal counts, including bank fraud, sanctions violations and conspiracy to steal trade secrets, while acquitting it of racketeering conspiracy and conspiracy to obstruct justice [8][5][11]. The verdict followed a trial lasting more than two months over allegations that Huawei misled banks about its Iran business and obtained technology from U.S. companies [8][39]. Prosecutors said Huawei concealed its Iran operations to preserve access to international banking and dollar-clearing services and pursued technology from competitors. The company argued that the government assembled isolated incidents into an unsupported corporate conspiracy. It has rejected the convictions and says it will appeal [28][8]. U.S. restrictions have already limited Huawei’s access to U.S. technology and telecom markets. The company continues to operate internationally and has expanded into chips [36][5]. U.S. District Judge Ann Donnelly is scheduled to sentence Huawei on September 14, 2027; potential penalties include fines, forfeiture and restitution [8][28].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

Huawei didn't steal its way to success

— Brian Heberlig, Huawei lawyer (The Hindu)

Key Points

  • Prosecutors said Huawei ran an internal program offering bonuses to employees who obtained industrial secrets from competitors [11].
  • Banking dispute: Huawei’s defense argued that HSBC and other banks knew about its Iran business and competed for the company’s account [30][8].
  • Defense case: Huawei lawyer Brian Heberlig pointed to $110 billion in research-and-development investment and $11.4 billion in technology licensing payments over two decades [42].
  • Trial scale: Prosecutors called more than 60 witnesses during the trial, while Huawei’s defense called 15 [8][5].
  • 5G restrictions: Before the verdict, Washington had urged countries not to use Huawei infrastructure for new 5G networks [11][50].

Perspectives

U.S. prosecutors: Brooklyn U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella described the verdict as accountability for what prosecutors called years of sanctions evasion, lies to banks and theft from U.S. technology companies [8].

Sources: Al-Monitor (Reuters)

Huawei: The company said the five trade-secret disputes cited by prosecutors had been resolved as civil matters over the past two decades and said no court had found it liable for willful misappropriation [15].

Sources: DW

Chinese government: Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing opposed U.S. efforts to suppress Chinese companies and supported their defense of their rights and interests [8].

Sources: Al-Monitor (Reuters)

Timeline

  • December 2018: Huawei CFO Meng Wanzhou was detained in Canada on a U.S. warrant [4].
  • January 2019: U.S. authorities publicly announced criminal charges against Huawei [39].
  • 2020: Prosecutors added allegations of trade-secret theft from U.S. technology companies [14].
  • 24 November 2026: Brooklyn jury convicted Huawei on 10 of 12 counts [8].
  • 14 September 2027: Judge Ann Donnelly is scheduled to sentence Huawei [8].

Industry Impact

  • German telecom networks: A 2024 agreement between Germany’s government and mobile operators bars Huawei components from core networks and parts of access-network control software from the end of 2026, with tighter requirements planned for 2029 [50].

Historical Background

U.S. authorities cited national-security concerns when they placed Huawei on a trade blacklist in 2019, restricting its access to U.S. technology [39][36]. Huawei Chief Financial Officer Meng Wanzhou later returned to China under a deferred prosecution agreement, and the charges against her were dropped [9].

item.content:encoded:
Saudi-led coalition strikes Yemen port after Houthis threaten Saudi ports

Category: World

A Saudi-led coalition supporting Yemen’s internationally recognized government said Wednesday it struck operational targets at Hodeidah port and sites in Saada and Amran after Yemen’s Houthi movement threatened to attack Jeddah and other Saudi Red Sea ports if Hodeidah was hit [13][11]. The exchange followed a Houthi drone strike Tuesday on a tower in Riyadh’s financial district, which Saudi authorities said injured 11 people [3][8]. Witnesses identified the Riyadh building as the 80-story Public Investment Fund Tower, headquarters of Saudi Arabia’s sovereign wealth fund. The same tower was hit on Nov. 19, causing damage but no reported injuries [6][10]. The Houthis had not claimed responsibility for Tuesday’s strike at the time of the reports, while the coalition blamed them and vowed a response [19][3]. Hodeidah is a main entry point for food and other essential imports into Houthi-controlled northern Yemen, where millions depend on imported supplies [13]. Local officials said a separate coalition strike on buses and trucks in Lahj province killed 26 people on Tuesday; government forces blamed the Houthis [1][10].

The port of Jeddah, along with all other Saudi enemy ports along the Red Sea coast, will become targets for our forces should the enemy carry out its threats to bombard the port of Hodeidah

— Yahya Saree, Houthi military spokesman (NDTV)

Key Points

  • Port warnings: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree called on workers and nearby residents to evacuate, and urged shipping companies to withdraw vessels from Saudi Red Sea ports [13][11].
  • Sanctions announced: Britain imposed an asset freeze on the Houthi group and asset freezes and travel bans on four senior figures, citing attempts to undermine stability [19][1].

Perspectives

Saudi-led coalition: Coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki called the Riyadh strike a “cowardly terrorist attack” and said authorities were inspecting the site [21].

Sources: Gulf Times and Al-Monitor

Timeline

  • 8 November 2026: A Houthi strike hit an Aramco building in Riyadh’s financial district [30][16]
  • 19 November 2026: The PIF Tower was struck, damaging the building but causing no reported injuries [10][3]
  • 24 November 2026: A second tower strike injured 11 people in Riyadh’s financial district [29][8]
  • 25 November 2026: Houthis threatened Saudi ports; coalition said it struck Hodeidah and other targets [13][11]

Industry Impact

  • Aviation and events: Attacks on Riyadh infrastructure led to a two-week suspension of airport flights and cancellations of international events, including the Future Investment Initiative conference [1][19].
  • Saudi investment district: The strike hit the PIF Tower in King Abdullah Financial District, which also houses the Saudi stock exchange and offices of international firms including Goldman Sachs [6][21].

Historical Background

The Saudi-led coalition intervened in Yemen in early 2015 after the Houthis captured Sanaa and the internationally recognized government fled to Aden [1][19]. The war caused hundreds of thousands of deaths and a humanitarian catastrophe before an uneasy ceasefire took effect in 2022 [1][32]. Fighting resumed in July 2026, with reports linking its resumption to the wider U.S.-Iran war [3][14].

International Reactions

  • 🇮🇳 India: India condemned the Riyadh strike and other attacks on Saudi civilian, economic and energy infrastructure, and said its embassy was assisting injured Indian nationals [8].
  • 🇵🇰 Pakistan: Pakistan denounced the attack, voiced solidarity with Saudi Arabia and said the kingdom had the right to defend its territory [10].

Travel Advisory

  • India’s embassy asked Indian nationals in Saudi Arabia to follow local rules and regulations, while authorities restricted access to some streets in Riyadh’s financial district [22][32].

Q&A

Q: What other Saudi sites have been hit in the current escalation?

A: An Aramco building in Riyadh was struck earlier in November; an October attack on King Khalid International Airport killed 14 people [30][1].

item.content:encoded:
China docks Shenzhou-24 at Tiangong with Pakistan's first astronaut

Category: World

China’s Shenzhou-24 spacecraft docked with the Tiangong space station on Wednesday, carrying Pakistan Air Force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, the first foreign astronaut to join a Chinese crewed mission. The spacecraft arrived at 11:56 a.m. Beijing time, three hours and 38 minutes after launching from Jiuquan aboard a Long March-2F rocket [9][17]. Ali will spend about a week aboard Tiangong as a payload specialist, then return to Earth aboard Shenzhou-23 with two departing crew members. The Shenzhou-24 crew, led by Chinese astronaut Tang Hongbo and including flight engineer Wu Yi, will conduct more than 90 scientific experiments and technology tests [9][2][4]. The flight is the first to carry a foreign astronaut on a Chinese crewed spacecraft and Pakistan’s first crewed orbital mission. Ali is due to conduct four joint China-Pakistan experiments. Tang and Wu will remain on the station for a six-month rotation, while Shenzhou-23 astronaut Zhu Yangzhu is staying for a year to study long-duration spaceflight [9][17][24][21].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

I want to assure you that I am not flying for myself. I carry the name of Pakistan on my shoulder, the hopes of 250 million Pakistanis.

— Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, Pakistani astronaut and Pakistan Air Force pilot (Firstpost)

Did you know: Pakistani adventurer Namira Salim flew on a Virgin Galactic suborbital mission in 2023, a flight that did not complete an orbit around Earth [45][10].

Key Points

  • Docking method: Shenzhou-24 used an autonomous 3.5-hour rendezvous and docking mode; controllers can switch to a five-hour or longer approach if needed for safety [17].
  • Repair mechanism: Researchers will test whether solar heating outside the cabin can restore the mechanical properties of self-healing carbon-fiber composites after microcracks form [17].
  • Crew handover: The departing Shenzhou-23 crew includes Lai Ka-ying, Hong Kong’s first astronaut, and Zhang Zhiyuan [13][14].
  • Seed samples: The quinoa study will expose 32 seed samples outside the station to assess how microgravity and cosmic radiation affect seed longevity and nutritional properties [17].
  • Microbe study: Proposed by Pakistan’s Space and Upper Atmosphere Research Commission (SUPARCO), the cyanobacteria test will run in the station’s life-ecology experiment cabinet [17].
  • Rocket safeguards: China’s Long March-2F team made 12 technical improvements for the flight, including a manual backup channel for separating the rocket from its launch tower [17].
  • Training demands: Mission commander Tang Hongbo said language and cultural differences complicated joint preparation; Ali trained in Beijing for seven months and learned Mandarin [25][15].
  • Mission record: The flight also makes Tang Hongbo the first astronaut to visit Tiangong three times, after earlier missions aboard Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 [33][45].
  • Pakistan’s ambitions: Pakistan has no spacecraft of its own for sending astronauts to orbit, and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has said he hopes a Pakistani astronaut will eventually reach the Moon [24][26].
  • Research projects: Pakistan’s space agency says Ali’s work includes cultivating microalgae as a potential source of food and oxygen and testing how spaceflight affects quinoa seeds [9][46].

Perspectives

Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif: Sharif called the mission a source of national pride and said it could inspire Pakistani young people and extend cooperation with China into space [19].

Sources: ClickOrlando

Chinese President Xi Jinping: Xi described China’s space station as a “boat” for peace, friendship and cooperation, and said Beijing was willing to deepen international space cooperation [19].

Sources: ClickOrlando

Blaine Curcio, founder of Orbital Gateway Consulting: Curcio said the mission brings Pakistan prestige, scientific and technical know-how, deeper cooperation with China and diplomatic goodwill [21].

Sources: The Korea Herald

Timeline

  • February 2025: China and Pakistan signed a bilateral space cooperation agreement [2][45]
  • April 2026: Muhammad Zeeshan Ali was selected as one of Pakistan’s astronaut candidates [41]
  • May 2026: Shenzhou-23 carried the current station crew to Tiangong [3][24]
  • 25 November 2026: Shenzhou-24 docked at Tiangong after its morning launch from Jiuquan [9][17]
  • February 2025: China and Pakistan signed the spaceflight cooperation agreement [11][19]
  • 24 November 2026: Chinese officials introduced the three-person Shenzhou-24 crew [47][34]
  • 25 November 2026: Shenzhou-24 launched from Jiuquan aboard a Long March-2F rocket [11][28]
  • 25 November 2026: The spacecraft docked at Tiangong’s Tianhe core module [17][50]

Technical Details

  • Rapid rendezvous: Shenzhou-24 used the autonomous rapid rendezvous and docking mode, the fourth use of this mode by a Shenzhou spacecraft [3][17].
  • Rocket safety changes: The Long March-2F team made 12 technical improvements, including revised propellant-system seals and a manual backup channel for separating the rocket from the launch tower [17].

Scientific Significance

  • Potential life-support research: Findings from the cyanobacteria experiment could inform oxygen regeneration for future deep-space missions [17].
  • Crop-breeding applications: Quinoa results could help identify varieties suited to space cultivation and provide reference data for breeding on Earth [17].

Historical Background

Space cooperation between China and Pakistan dates to the early 1990s. China has launched Pakistani satellites, and a Pakistani-built rover is planned for a Chinese lunar mission around 2028 [21].

B.C. towns issue evacuation alerts as storm tides threaten coast

Category: Canada

Squamish declared a local state of emergency as communities across British Columbia issued evacuation alerts and closed waterfront areas Tuesday amid coastal flooding risks from king tides, storm surge and heavy rain. Squamish said the declaration would allow it to carry out flood-mitigation work. Parksville and the Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation warned shoreline residents to be ready to leave [2][8][6]. Environment Canada warned that tides could run 20 to 50 centimetres above the highest astronomical tides through Thursday. Forecasts called for up to 225 millimetres of rain on parts of Vancouver Island, wind gusts up to 90 km/h in Greater Victoria and rapidly rising rivers across Vancouver Island and the South Coast [4][2]. The alerts cover coastal areas from Metro Vancouver and Vancouver Island to Haida Gwaii and the central and Sunshine coasts. Victoria closed sections of its Dallas Road waterfront seawall, and Ucluelet closed beaches and trails. The province increased highway patrols and warned that debris or flooding could force sudden road closures [5][8][9].

Primary Source: View original article

Usually we'll get king tides, but not with a very big storm. So, this is the first time I've seen a king tide with a big storm.

— Geoff Heith, photographer and filmmaker from Port Hardy (Times Colonist)

Key Points

  • Highway preparations: Contractors are clearing debris from roadways and drainage infrastructure and are ready to respond [9]
  • River conditions: The B.C. River Forecast Centre said peak flows could reach levels associated with a two- to five-year return period, with some weather scenarios indicating higher flows [2]
  • Parksville alert: The evacuation alert includes two RV resorts, a curling club, the community park, three resort or hotel properties and two Sutherland Crescent addresses; residents were told to prepare to leave on short notice [10]

Perspectives

District of Squamish: The district said declaring a local state of emergency gives it the legal authority to complete flood-mitigation work under B.C.’s Emergency and Disaster Management Act [2].

Sources: Times Colonist

Delta Mayor Melissa Granum: Granum said city staff know which homes have less protection and where to direct support during storm surges [8].

Sources: CBC News

Tla-o-qui-aht First Nation: The First Nation urged shoreline residents to take precautions and be ready to evacuate, but said it did not expect significant impacts at the time [4].

Sources: The Globe and Mail

Timeline

  • 24 November 2026: Squamish set up a sandbag pickup station, while crews built barriers to protect downtown [8]
  • 25 November 2026: Parksville scheduled a morning update on its shoreline evacuation alert [10]
  • 26 November 2026: The highest tides in the Sea-to-Sky region were forecast for Thursday morning [2]

Historical Background

A storm and king tide caused significant damage to Vancouver’s Jericho Pier in November 2021 and left a barge stranded at Sunset Beach for more than a year. In January 2022, another storm-and-tide combination damaged the Stanley Park seawall and Kitsilano Pool [5].

Travel Advisory

  • Road safety: Check DriveBC for current conditions before travelling [9].
  • Coastal access: Stay away from closed waterfront pathways and coastlines, and follow municipal updates [8][5].

Q&A

Q: Which routes could face closures?

A: The provincial advisory named Highway 101 communities on the Sunshine Coast, Howe Sound, Metro Vancouver, the Malahat, and west-coast Vancouver Island routes near Port Renfrew, Tofino, Ucluelet and Gold River [9].

Canada has not made a final decision on its F-35 order, which has been under review for more than a year [3][1].

item.content:encoded:
Alberta plans Sovereignty Act motion against federal hate speech law

Category: Canada

Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said Nov. 24 her government will introduce a motion under the province’s Sovereignty Act opposing the removal of a Criminal Code defence for good-faith opinions on religious subjects under the federal Combatting Hate Act. The federal law took effect July 18. Smith says the change could deter lawful religious and political speech; Ottawa says the Charter protects religious expression and the law targets intentional promotion of hatred [1][3][6]. The proposed motion would ask Alberta’s cabinet to consider further lawful steps, rather than directly cancel the federal law. Alberta Justice Minister Mickey Amery already has authority over whether many hate-speech charges proceed in the province. Constitutional law professor Gerard Kennedy said the motion could guide police and prosecutors but not bind them. The federal law also created offences targeting intimidation outside religious or cultural institutions and the public display of certain hate or terrorist symbols [1][2][4].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

The federal government, yes, has the constitutional authority to define what areas they believe should be in the Criminal Code

— Mickey Amery, Alberta justice minister (The Globe and Mail)

Key Points

  • Prosecution authority: Alberta said it recorded 14 cases involving hate-crime offences in 2025-26; Amery had no comparable figures for the period since the federal act took effect [2].
  • Provincial guidance: Amery directed Alberta Crown prosecutors in September to give significant weight to freedom of expression and not charge people simply for controversial or unpopular political or religious beliefs [6][1].
  • Party politics: Alberta NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi called the move political theatre ahead of the United Conservative Party’s annual meeting in Calgary, while Smith denied it was aimed at the gathering [1][4].
  • Faith leaders: Edmonton Rabbi Ari Drelich said open disagreement should be protected, but speech that could lead to violence presents a serious problem [1].

Perspectives

Alberta Justice Minister Mickey Amery said the province is not planning a court challenge, describing the motion as Alberta “drawing a constitutional line” [3].

Sources: The Globe and Mail

Federal Justice Minister Sean Fraser’s office said the law responds to calls for stronger protections against hate-motivated crime and gives law enforcement stronger tools to protect communities [1][2].

Sources: CBC News

Cardus president Brian Dijkema warned Alberta against attempting to override federal law and urged respect for the Constitution’s divisions of power [3].

Sources: The Globe and Mail

Alberta NDP Leader Naheed Nenshi argued Smith should lobby Ottawa if she wants the federal law changed, rather than pursue a provincial motion [4].

Sources: The Canadian Press, republished by SooToday

Timeline

  • 2022: Alberta enacted the Sovereignty within a United Canada Act [1][3]
  • 18 July 2026: Federal Combatting Hate Act took effect, removing the religious-opinion defence [6][3]
  • August 2026: Smith and Alberta’s public safety minister criticized an Edmonton police post encouraging people to report hate crimes [4]
  • 24 November 2026: Smith announced a motion challenging the federal law’s effects [1][4]

Historical Background

Smith has previously used the Sovereignty Act to push back against proposed federal environmental regulations and to direct provincial law-enforcement agencies not to enforce Ottawa’s gun buyback program. In a recent provincial referendum, nearly 56 per cent of Albertans rejected giving provincial law priority when it conflicts with federal law [3].

Q&A

Q: When will Alberta’s motion be debated?

A: The Globe and Mail reported that the motion had not yet been tabled and did not specify a debate date [3].

item.content:encoded:
Ottawa seeks faster land seizures for Toronto-Quebec City rail line

Category: Canada

Canada’s federal government has proposed giving Alto, the Crown corporation developing a high-speed rail line between Toronto and Quebec City, expanded powers to acquire land through expropriation without public hearings and transfer property directly to a private consortium [2][1]. Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon said the measures would prevent land acquisition disputes from delaying the project for years and argued they do not remove due process [1][3]. The proposals, included in a Budget 2026 motion published Nov. 20, would exempt Alto from the federal Expropriation Act and parts of several rail and environmental laws [2][6]. The project is expected to cost $60 billion to $90 billion; construction of its first phase, between Montreal and Ottawa, is scheduled to begin in 2029 or 2030 [1][3]. Farmers, opposition politicians and municipal representatives have raised concerns about property rights, farmland and consultation, while Alto says it will pay fair compensation and limit the impacts [2][6].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

There is no removal of due process

— Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon (The Globe and Mail)

Key Points

  • Property restrictions: The proposed rules could let the transport minister prohibit work on affected land for four years and preserve a government right of first refusal for as long as eight years [2].
  • Crossing disputes: Where the rail corridor splits farms or roads, the proposal would send disputes to private arbitration, with each party potentially paying up to $25,000 plus its own legal costs [2][1].
  • Farm impacts: Alto’s Montreal-Ottawa segment would cross about 1,700 properties, including roughly 500 agricultural properties, according to Alto’s chief executive [1].
  • Projected benefits: A study commissioned by Alto estimates the operating line could generate about $24.5 billion in annual economic benefits [2].

Perspectives

Avi Lewis, NDP leader: Lewis criticized the project’s public-private ownership model, saying smaller communities feel excluded and insufficiently consulted, and argued major projects need a transparent, democratic process [1].

Sources: The Globe and Mail

Martin Caron, president of the Union des producteurs agricoles: Caron argued that bypassing ordinary expropriation rules could restrict challenges, and said the farmers’ organization is campaigning against the rail project [4].

Sources: Le Devoir

Yves-François Blanchet, Bloc Québécois leader: Blanchet warned that the powers could extend to provincial government land and properties associated with Crown-owned utility Hydro-Québec, and called the proposal excessive [4].

Sources: Le Devoir

Timeline

  • March 2026: Parliament passed the High-Speed Rail Network Act with limited acquisition exceptions [2]
  • 20 November 2026: Budget motion detailed broader proposed land acquisition powers [2][6]
  • 24 November 2026: MacKinnon defended the proposals before a cabinet meeting in Ottawa [1][3]
  • 2029 or 2030: Construction of the Montreal-Ottawa first phase is expected to begin [1][3]

Technical Details

  • Grade-separated crossings: With trains travelling at speeds of up to 300 km/h, crossings must use overpasses or underpasses rather than meet the tracks at road level, and the corridor would need to be fenced [2].
  • Work prohibitions: A proposed notice could prohibit significant construction or improvements on a targeted property for up to four years, and the legislation would exclude value added by such work from expropriation compensation [2].

Historical Background

Parliament’s High-Speed Rail Network Act, passed in March 2026, already allowed Alto to bypass upfront purchase negotiations and replace public hearings with written objections while retaining the federal Expropriation Act [2]. The latest draft would remove that remaining statutory framework and expand the project-specific exceptions [2][6].

Q&A

Q: What route options remain under consideration in eastern Ontario?

A: Alto is considering a direct Ottawa-Peterborough corridor and a more southerly route that could include Kingston as a stop [1].

item.description: The European Space Agency (ESA) has revised BepiColombo’s remaining maneuvers after a software fault cut short the joint European-Japanese mission’s Mercury orbit-insertion burn. item.content:encoded:
ESA revises BepiColombo maneuvers after Mercury insertion software fault

Category: Science

The European Space Agency (ESA) has revised BepiColombo’s remaining maneuvers after a software fault cut short the joint European-Japanese mission’s Mercury orbit-insertion burn. ESA says the revised sequence can correct the spacecraft’s trajectory without additional thruster burns, keeping the separation of its two science orbiters and the start of science operations on schedule [11][13][10]. The fault involved attitude guidance and thruster control, and the spacecraft entered a protective safe mode when the burn stopped. The spacecraft reached a stable Mercury orbit; ESA and its partners continue to investigate the software problem [4][11][8]. The European Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Japan’s Mio orbiter remain joined and are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10, with routine science operations planned for April 2027. The European orbiter is expected to reach its final orbit in March, while Mio will investigate Mercury’s magnetosphere [4][6][10].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

After each burn, the Flight Dynamics team determines the achieved orbit to then design the next manoeuvre

— Frank Budnik, ESA BepiColombo Flight Dynamics Manager (The Register)

Key Points

  • Orbit adjustment: The insertion burn achieved about 77% of its planned velocity change, leaving BepiColombo in a 75-hour orbit rather than the planned 58-hour orbit [11][4][13].
  • Two investigations: The European Mercury Planetary Orbiter carries 11 instruments to survey the planet, while Japan’s Mio orbiter carries five instruments focused on its magnetosphere [6].
  • Weak-stability capture: BepiColombo entered orbit using a technique involving a slower approach than typical planetary insertions. Previously, only some missions to the Moon had used the technique [6][9].
  • X-ray instrument: Before arrival, the MIXS X-ray instrument imaged the Crab Nebula to help scientists measure its angular resolution [6].

Timeline

  • October 2018: BepiColombo launched on its mission to Mercury [16]
  • 3 September 2026: The transfer module separated, exposing instruments for testing [16]
  • 9 December 2026: Mio and the European orbiter are scheduled to separate [10][11]
  • 16 December 2026: Mio’s protective sunshield is scheduled to detach [10][6]
  • 10 March 2027: The European orbiter is expected to reach its final orbit [10][16]
  • 6 April 2027: BepiColombo’s science phase is scheduled to begin [10][6]

Technical Details

  • Compact X-ray optics: MIXS focuses X-rays with micro-pore optics rather than conventional nested mirrors. Its pores are about 20 microns wide, allowing the instrument to measure one meter and weigh 11 kilograms [16].
  • Surface X-ray fluorescence: MIXS will measure X-rays emitted when solar X-rays or magnetospheric particles strike Mercury’s surface. Their characteristic energies can identify surface elements, and the instrument is designed to produce higher-resolution images than earlier missions [16].

Scientific Significance

  • Simultaneous measurements: The two orbiters will observe Mercury from different orbits, allowing scientists to compare measurements taken at the same time; project scientist Geraint Jones described this as unprecedented for Mercury exploration [14].
  • Hollows research: Scientists hope to investigate Mercury’s mysterious surface hollows, which may form as volatile substances are driven off by intense solar heat [2].

Historical Background

Underperforming transfer-module thrusters in 2024 forced ESA and the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency to revise BepiColombo’s route and delay its planned arrival [1]. The spacecraft’s journey included gravity-assist flybys of Earth, Venus and Mercury to reduce its speed before orbit insertion [9][16].

COP31 ends without political pact as countries pursue voluntary climate initiatives

Category: Science

The COP31 climate summit in Antalya ended on Nov. 22 without an overarching political agreement after countries split over whether the final text should address fossil fuels and increase climate finance [1][8]. Governments also pursued several voluntary initiatives outside the main negotiations [5][1]. More than 80 countries backed a target to raise electricity’s share of global energy use to 35% by 2035, while the Utilities for Net Zero Alliance outlined plans for $156 billion in annual grid investment [1][8]. The pledge does not specify that the additional electricity must come from renewable or other low-carbon sources [3]. Delegates also agreed to continue climate-finance talks through 2028, without setting a new amount or baseline for increasing adaptation funding [15]. A regional Pacific roadmap for moving away from fossil fuels is expected by July 2027, ahead of COP32, scheduled for Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, the following year [1][15].

Primary Source: View original article

Read more: Full article on Kite Static

If we fail on climate, the inequities we see today will grow almost beyond imagining: widespread crop failures, people losing access to water, rising conflict over basic resources, mass migration and growing tensions between countries

— Katharine Hayhoe, climate scientist at The Nature Conservancy (PBS NewsHour)

Key Points

  • Energy roadmaps: Twenty-seven governments had published or committed to publish plans for transitioning away from fossil fuels, while eight more announced plans during COP31 [1][8].
  • Treaty proposal: Thirty countries said they were working on a proposal for an international treaty to limit fossil-fuel production [1][3].
  • Building efficiency: A voluntary buildings initiative backed by 24 countries aims to cut energy use per square metre by 25% by 2035 [15].
  • Geothermal target: The Global Geothermal Ambition 2050 plan aims to increase global geothermal electricity and heat supply to 12 times its 2025 level [15].
  • Methane: Governments agreed to intensify efforts to cut methane emissions, including from fossil-fuel production, and establish new international partnerships [15].

Perspectives

European Union and Ireland: Irish climate minister Darragh O’Brien said a pact omitting fossil fuels and a transition away from them was unacceptable; the EU and several other countries rejected the proposed text [9][15].

Sources: Daily Maverick

Saudi Arabia: Saudi Arabia defended carbon capture as a practical climate response, a position that would allow continued reliance on oil and gas, according to the account of the closing negotiations [9].

Sources: Daily Maverick

Chlöe Swarbrick, Green Party co-leader: Swarbrick said a deal that glossed over fossil fuels would have been a “sham” and urged New Zealand’s government to support including them in the text [14].

Sources: Scoop

Tasneem Essop, executive director of Climate Action Network International: Essop blamed developed countries for the failed talks, saying wealthy nations had gutted measures that could have protected people from worsening climate impacts [2].

Sources: PBS NewsHour

Timeline

  • 2023: COP28 decision called for transitioning away from fossil fuels in energy systems [8]
  • April 2026: Countries held the first conference on transitioning away from fossil fuels [1]
  • 22 November 2026: COP31 concluded after negotiations failed to produce an overarching political agreement [1][8]
  • July 2027: Tuvalu and Ireland are due to host the next transition-away conference [1]
  • 2027: Ethiopia is set to host COP32 in Addis Ababa [1][15]

Technical Details

  • Carbon-removal scale: An early draft called for carbon-dioxide capture and removal to reach at least 551 million tonnes by 2035, then 1.4 billion to 2.8 billion tonnes annually; projects operating or in development are forecast to fall short of even the lower target [3].
  • Capture-project record: A review cited in the COP31 coverage found that 88% of carbon capture and storage projects from 1972 to 2018 failed because of technical or financial complications [3].

Scientific Significance

  • Warming outlook: A Climate Action Tracker report said progress in slowing warming had essentially stalled over the previous five years; even if countries meet their stated plans, the world would reach about 2.6°C above pre-industrial levels by the century’s end [2].
  • Carbon-removal risks: Some proposed approaches could require extensive land for growing plants, raising concerns about land grabs and displacement, while ocean-based carbon storage may pose ecological risks [3].

Historical Background

The 2015 Paris Agreement set the goal of keeping global warming well below 2°C while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5°C [6]. At COP28 in 2023, countries agreed for the first time to call for a transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems [8][5]. COP31 was the first climate summit since Copenhagen in 2009 to end without a final agreement, according to accounts of the negotiations [1][9].

Q&A

Q: What separate funding mechanism did delegates agree to for the Adaptation Fund?

A: The UN Adaptation Fund is to receive a direct share of proceeds from international carbon-credit trading under Article 6.4 of the Paris Agreement [15].
